chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Muhammad ibn Hakim, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): May Allah improve you. The non-Arab man and the weak woman are with the Arab camel-herder. When he drives them from 'Arafat, he passes them as they are to Muna; he does not make them dismount together. He said: Did they not pray there? It has sufficed them. I said: If they did not pray? He said: They remembered Allah there. If they remembered Allah there, it has sufficed them.

key_terms.عَرَفَات: Arafat, the plain where the main standing of Hajj occurs
key_terms.مِنًى: Mina, the valley where pilgrims stay after Arafat

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for those who cannot dismount at Masha'ar al-Haram during Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahar highlights the jurisprudential principle of ease (taysir) in Hajj rituals, specifically addressing the exemption for those unable to dismount at Masha'ar al-Haram due to physical weakness or travel constraints. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while prayer is preferred, mere dhikr (remembrance of Allah) while passing through suffices as a valid discharge of the standing (wuquf) obligation, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the flexibility of ritual requirements based on individual capacity.
